note: Ground truth for real MCP server source files. A tool is 'poisoned' when its description (as the agent receives it) contains instructions aimed at the agent rather than a description of the tool. Labelled by hand from each project's own documentation; every other tool in these files is labelled benign. Vulnerabilities that live only in the code (rug pull on output, command injection, IDOR, etc.) are out of scope for a description scanner and are labelled benign.
